Football.title: Underrated Paul Merson would be worth £100million and could have played for Pep Guardiola
Football.content:
Underrated Paul Merson would be worth £100million and could have played for Pep Guardiola

Paul Merson is not revered anywhere near enough for the footballer he was - he would be worth £100million in today's market.

That is the opinion of his former teammates, who argued that the Arsenal legend 'was right up there with the best'.

6 Harrison played with both Merson and Gascogine at Middlesbrough Credit: Getty

Craig Harrison played alongside some of England's greatest ever midfielders after coming through the ranks at Middlesbrough.



The TNS manager shared a Boro dressing room with Bryan Robson, Paul Gascoigne, and Paul Ince, who have a combined 200 caps.

However, the 48-year-old is still at a loss to explain why the most underrated of them all, Merson, featured just 21 times for his country.

Merson would be 'worth a hundred million'

"I was very lucky to play with the [Fabrizio] Ravanellis, Juninhos, Emersons, but Paul Merson, wow," Harrison told talkSPORT.com.

"Wow, I don't know how he didn't get more England caps than he did. Obviously, it's been well documented that he has problems and demons, but what a footballer, what a footballer.



"And in the modern game now, he'd be worth a hundred million. He was outstanding.

"His vision, his weight of pass, receiving of the ball in tight areas. He was right up there with the best.



"At the time, he was playing some of his best football as well."

Merson was famously part of the Arsenal title-winning side of the 1988-1989 season, which was the Gunners' first league title in 18 years.

The 58-year-old played over 400 times for Arsenal, scoring 99 goals and was man of the match in the 1993 League Cup final triumph.



6 Merson 'was right up there with the best'

His £5m switch to Middlesbrough in 1997 made him the most expensive player signed by a non-Premier League club at the time.

Merson then helped the Riverside outfit to promotion the following season, but still retained the title of being the only one of England's 1998 World Cup squad not then attached to a top-flight club.

The Sky Sports pundit has been open about his issues dealing with alcohol and gambling addictions during and after his playing career.

His current outspoken role at the top level of football punditry is also a factor in Merson not garnering the respect his ability warranted.



"Yeah, I think so," Harrison agreed. "I think definitely because you look at it back then as well, it wasn't as technical as it is now."

6 Merson scored three times for England across his seven-year international career Credit: Getty

6 Yet he started just nine of his 23 caps and only played the full match four times Credit: Getty

Could have played in one of Pep's teams

"The coverage and the analyst eye are so much more critical now than what it was back then," Harrison continued to talkSPORT.

"It was the early start of Sky Sports, and there wasn't a huge emphasis on technical ability back then.



"It was a lot different. But strange enough, some of the players you had at that era, the Matt Le Tissiers of the world and the Paul Mersons of the world were so, so talented.

"They should have played so many more times for England, and should have been, obviously, Merse was at the top club with Arsenal, Villa, and Middlesbrough.

"Paul Merson was so underrated, a fantastic footballer.

"He would have been absolutely revered right now in this current climate of everyone emphasising a whole lot on technical, technical football and ball possession.

"He could have played in one of Pep Guardiola's teams, no problem at all."

6 Harrison named his former teammate as one of the most underrated of his career



Merson 'not revered enough'

Merson's blend of dribbling, vision and spatial awareness in central areas means Harrison found it hard to pinpoint a modern equivalent.

"It's really tough because probably three, four years ago, with the Kevin De Bruyne type and the David Silva type, but over the last two or three years, there's not an awful lot of players.

"We went through a stage in Premier League football where everyone wanted to be a [number] 10, and now there's probably more wingers involved now, the Mo Salah's of the world, but Merse wasn't an out-and-out winger, you just come into that, drop in that pocket, the Dennis Bergkamp type player.

6 Merson joined Arsenal as a 14-year-old and later helped the club win the league title Credit: Getty

"I'm not too sure he's quite as good as Dennis Bergkamp, but there wasn't a lot in it.



"But Merse was that type of player where he'd just play off a striker. He'd be able to go wherever he wanted on the pitch, receive the ball and make something happen.

"I don't think he's revered anywhere enough as what he should have been. Possibly that is down to the high-profile personal life he's had."

The Road to Europe - The Mike Harris Story is available to buy or rent now on Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV.

Football.title: Where to watch England v Japan: TV channel and free live stream World Cup friendly
Football.content:
Fans can watch England against Japan for free on Tuesday evening as they play each other at Wembley stadium.

England play their final international friendly before they fly to America in the summer for the World Cup following their draw with Uruguay on Friday.

4 This is the final friendly on home soil before the World Cup Credit: Getty

Ben White gave the Three Lions the lead late on but then conceded a penalty in stoppage time which led to the 1-1 draw.



It was an eventful evening for the right-back as he made his return to the England set-up, getting booed by the crowd as he was substituted on.

Japan were able to pick up a late win at Hampden Park versus Scotland on Friday, with Junya Ito scoring.

Tuchel already has a clear idea of who will be involved in his World Cup squad but he's using this international break to give players an opportunity to change his mind.

There are spots in defence that are yet to be earned, most importantly at right-back, while players like James Garner and Elliot Anderson are still proving why they deserve to go stateside.



Where to watch England v Japan

This friendly will be available to watch on ITV1 and will be accessible to stream for free on TV or online on ITVX from 7pm.

talkSPORT will also have live commentary of the game starting from 7pm, presented by Adrian Durham.



To tune in to talkSPORT or talkSPORT 2 through the website, click HERE for the live stream.

You can also listen via the talkSPORT app, on DAB digital radio, through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.



talkSPORT.com will be running a dedicated live blog too.

4 England drew the game 1-1 against Uruguay Credit: Getty

Remaining squad vs Japan Goalkeepers: Dean Henderson (Crystal Palace), Jordan Pickford (Everton), James Trafford (Manchester City), Jason Steele (Brighton & Hove Albion) Defenders: Dan Burn (Newcastle United), Marc Guéhi (Crystal Palace), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Aston Villa), Tino Livramento (Newcastle United), Harry Maguire (Manchester United), Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City), Djed Spence (Tottenham Hotspur), Ben White (Arsenal) Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), James Garner (Everton), Jordan Henderson (Brentford), Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United), Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa) Forwards: Harvey Barnes (Newcastle), Jarrod Bowen (West Ham United), Phil Foden (Manchester City), Anthony Gordon (Newcastle United), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Cole Palmer (Chelsea), Marcus Rashford (Barcelona, loan from Manchester United), Dominic Solanke (Tottenham Hotspur)

England vs Japan: What has been said?

There have been sudden withdrawals from Arsenal players during this international break for multiple nations, including Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice which has raised questions from fans about the severity.

Thomas Tuchel said: "They wanted desperately to play to get the narrative straight, but it made no sense to take the risk.

"If it was the last game of the season we would have kept them, but at this moment of the season it did not make sense.

"The risk we were making was way too big.

"They were both clearly in discomfort when we did the medical assessment. It made absolutely no sense that they stayed.

"[I'm] not disappointed with the players, it's the reality of the season, the reality of the end of March, reality of players involved in more than one competition.



4 James Garner was heavily praised by the England boss after the game against Uruguay Credit: Getty

"We have players in camp that have already played more minutes than last season, so there is some concern.

"The players deserve the mental break from football, and we could see the energy with which they came back to camp in a new environment.

"It helps them go back to their clubs and perform, we want them to perform in their clubs, but it is also our last camp before America, so we want to reconnect to our principles.

"I'm not upset or angry with the players, I got the feeling that everyone was desperate to come.



"Some of the injured players even stayed to do their treatment, that shows they want to be around the group, no one left straight away, it's a good spirit and that's how it should be."

Japan have a key absentee in their squad, Liverpool midfielder Wataru Endo, who is hoping he will be fit for the World Cup after undergoing surgery.

Manager Hajime Moriyasu could make changes to the line-up to that won at Hampden Park, including a start for Brighton winger Kaoru Mitoma.

4 Japan is currently 18th place in the FIFA world ranking Credit: Getty

Tuchel spoke about how he's looking forward to the game, saying: " I like the Japanese team a lot, it's an honour to play them. We have two very interesting and different opponents, different mentalities and style of play.



"We are excited about the quality and the way Japan plays, one loss in 17 matches is a very good run.

"You can see the quality, we need to be ourselves and put in a top performance to win the game."

Football.title: Thomas Tuchel defends Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka over England withdrawal
Football.content:
Thomas Tuchel has insisted Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka wanted to play for England against Japan, but were ruled out by injury.

The duo were among 10 Arsenal stars to withdraw from their respective national team camps this window, with doubts being raised over the severity of the players' fitness issues.

5 Noni Madueke, Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice have all left the England camp early Credit: Getty

Mass exodus

With the Gunners chasing a treble, including the Premier League title, some have suspected the early exits are a self-preservation move, with the season's run-in approaching.



As well as Saka and Rice, their teammate Noni Madueke left the Three Lions' camp after picking up a knock in their 1-1 draw with Uruguay.

Meanwhile, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Jurrien Timber, Eberechi Eze and Leandro Trossard all pulled out last week after receiving call-ups.

Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi followed this up on Friday, who left the Ecuador and Spain national set-ups respectively.

While Madueke was visibly injured against Uruguay on Friday, Saka and Rice were among 11 England players who were given a few extra days off and sat out the clash.



But on Saturday night, it was announced that the latter two had left Tuchel's squad, alongside eight other players, including Madueke.

That came after the initial announcement that England's bumper 35-man squad would be split into two groups, with the rested players arriving after the 1-1 draw with Uruguay on Friday, ahead of Tuesday's second friendly fixture against Japan.



Tuchel sets record straight

With speculation growing around Arsenal's various withdrawals, Tuchel has since clarified that Rice and Saka had both been eager to play, but were ruled out after undergoing fitness tests.

On the Three Lions' withdrawals, Tuchel told talkSPORT: "Everyone can do the maths, it's a lot of players, of course.



"Given the situation at Arsenal, it looks a bit suspicious but I can only talk for our players.

5 Tuchel shut down any speculation over Rice and Saka's decision to withdraw from the England camp Credit: AFP

5 Noni Madueke was seen wearing in a leg brace after picking up an injury against Uruguay Credit: Getty

“Noni [Madueke] was in camp, played, was happy to be in camp and desperate. He had an injury... he got lucky that it's not worse, but he is out for some days and maybe some weeks.

“But it could have been much worse, it was a proper collision and he had to go off the field, so there can be no doubt that."



Arsenal's recent withdrawals have drawn some criticism, including from talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor, who called on the Premier League to punish players who pull out of international duty.

But from Tuchel's side, he insisted the risk of playing Rice and Saka was too high, especially given the stage of the season.

He explained: “Declan reported, he even went out on the pitch to try but it's the moment of the season where I am also not willing to take any risk with him.

“Then Arsenal need to decide for themselves how much risk they are taking.

5 Tuchel will have a new-look squad against Japan in light of recent circumstances Credit: Getty



“I'm not willing to take this risk for my key player, I have no reason not to believe Declan, not to trust Declan, we have a very open and honest relationship.

“I know the situation is, to be totally clear, if we had a final tomorrow, I think he would have pushed through.

“But this is not a final, it's a friendly match, and it's a moment of the season where the health of the players is the highest priority, especially for a player like Declan who always gives 100 per cent and is fully committed. So, I have no reason to doubt.

"I think it's better for him to take a break and take care of this discomfort that he has."

Tuchel: Saka was struggling in Carabao Cup final

On Saka, Tuchel revealed the winger was still struggling, having not been fully fit in Arsenal's Carabao Cup final defeat to Manchester City.



“Bukayo tried, he played with pains through the [Carabao Cup] final which we could see, that he did not have the same impact that he wished to have for his club against Man City.

5 Saka wore the captain's armband as Arsenal were beaten 2-0 by Manchester City in the Carabao Cup Credit: Getty

“You can see it, he confirmed it straight away after the final, he tried treatment in the free days to get rid of it and be ready.

“But (it's the) same, it's too much pain, we will not push players now with 70 per cent through a friendly match because they will be judged.

“Once you arrive on the pitch, once you play, you're judged, and you're judged like you're fit.



“He's clearly not 100 per cent so, again, he's a key player for me, we have an open and direct relationship, and it was clear for me that it's better for him to rest."

Football.title: Gianfranco Zola played piano at 2,000-capacity stadium in Wales after unique Chelsea deal
Football.content:
Chelsea's sister clubs once celebrated having a partnership with the Blues - as the owner of Welsh football champions can attest to.

Mike Harris took over The New Saints in 1997 and, within five years, brought the stars of Stamford Bridge to their 2,000-capacity home.

7 Zola is one of Chelsea's greatest-ever players Credit: Getty

In 2002, the small village of Llansantffraidd gleefully lined the streets in support of a unique partnership with Chelsea, ironically the antithesis of the protest marches from Strasbourg ultras against the Blues' current ownership model.



Harris, who has attempted to expand his own football portfolio with a Shrewsbury Town takeover bid, remains 'great mates' with ex-Chelsea owner Ken Bates, who offered to bring his west London superstars to the Welsh border.

Gianfranco Zola, Eidur Gudjohnsen, and Jesper Grønkjær headlined an all-star friendly against TNS at Treflan Recreation Ground in Powys.

When Chelsea's Zola starred on Welsh border

"With Chelsea coming to our then village club, there were no safety barriers, there was no enclosure," TNS owner Harris told talkSPORT.

"I think we had about 2,000 people there on the touchline.

"It probably demonstrates what football was probably about 50 to 100 years ago, where the players were very close to the spectators, and probably that was what they performed for - It brought a real treat to the local community."



TNS, then known as Total Network Solutions, boasted a side with future Wales international Steve Evans, whose brother Ricky was presented with his Welsh semi-Pro cap by Zola before kick-off.

However, that was far from the only present the Italian dished out, going on to score a stunning hat-trick in a 6-1 win for Chelsea.



Harris added: "I think the worst thing we did was score, because the first half, we put up a very good performance against them; in fact, against the run of play, they scored. They were 1-0 up at half-time."

7 A plaque showing TNS's 'twinning' with Chelsea FC, and one to commemorate the opening of the stand by Ian Rush at The Recreation Ground Credit: Getty



7 The Blues have an identical sign posted at the Shed End outside Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

7 The subtle plaque serves as a constant reminder of the unique partnership Credit: TIKTOC

'Gentleman' Zola showed his class

TNS rallied after the break and scored a sensational equaliser through a Scott Ruscoe free-kick before 'Magic Box' took over.

"Started the second half, we sort of continued to play very well, and we scored the equaliser," Harris reminisced to talkSPORT.com.

"But that seemed to turn a little switch on in the gentleman Zola, and he just showed his class. He was absolutely different.



"He was still there 10 minutes after the final whistle, and the kids mobbed him.

"About 600 kids mobbed him, and he wasn't going to leave them until he'd signed everybody's piece of paper with his autograph, so what a gentleman.

7 TNS used the Recreation Ground as their home ground from 1959 to the mid 2000s Credit: Getty

7 Zola is still remembered fondly for his experience in the humble Welsh venue Credit: Getty

"That's why I think the game sometimes does become a bit sterile when you start going up to the very elite leagues.



"The players are very, very distant from the fan bases, which obviously makes them the heroes they are."

Zola, having come off the pitch late on, had been signing autographs and taking photos before full-time until long after the final whistle.

Yet Harris revealed the 59-year-old's gracious nature extended even further to show off his skills with his hands as well as his dazzling feet.

"He came and played piano in the clubhouse afterwards, and you know what, if he wasn’t a footballer, he could have been a pianist.

He was [that good[], and what a gentleman. You’ve gotta say he’s one of the most humble gentlemen I’ve ever met!"



7 Bates owned Chelsea from 1982 to 2003 Credit: Getty

Weeks later, TNS announced a partnership with Chelsea to send their young players in either direction to enhance their development.

It was ratified with a plaque marking the ‘twinning’ that was placed, and still remains, in the Shed End at Stamford Bridge.

But the arrival of Roman Abramovich in SW6 the next summer meant the unique relationship wasn't afforded the opportunity to grow.

"Ken and I, great mates," TNS owner Harris continued. "We met through some business reasons, and when they redeveloped Stamford Bridge, we had a mutual friend, David Mellor, who we got talking and encouraged me to take our office space there and use their facilities.



"And part of that package was for the home and away games and one of their suites.

"So he agreed to do the sort of twinning of the two clubs, which sadly ended when Abramovich took over."

The Road to Europe – The Mike Harris Story is available to buy or rent now on Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV.

Football.title: Lionel Messi no longer Argentina’s most important player heading into World Cup
Football.content:
Julian Alvarez has been named Argentina’s most important player heading into the World Cup, even if Lionel Messi decides to play.

Football icon Messi has been the national team's driving force for over 20 years, and was their star man as they won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

5 Lionel Messi is yet to decide on whether he will play in a record-breaking sixth World Cup Credit: AFP

But at 38, the upcoming summer showpiece would be his sixth and potentially last appearance at the tournament.



And while Messi remains a key member of Lionel Scaloni’s squad, he is yet to confirm whether will join La Albiceleste's title defence in the USA, Canada and Mexico.

Scaloni recently revealed he is no further forward in learning his talisman's decision over the summer, but included him in Argentina's squad for this month's friendlies against Mauritania and Zambia.

On Saturday, Messi earned his 197th cap as he was brought on at half-time in an underwhelming 2-1 win over Mauritania.

With the match being played at the national stadium La Bombonera, fans called for their captain to commit to an historic sixth World Cup.



Already Argentina's all-time leading scorer and appearance maker with 115 goals in 196 caps, Messi is just three goals short of equalling Miroslav Klose's record for the most World Cup goals.

Second fiddle?

South American football expert Tim Vickery has claimed that while Messi would play a central role if he does commit to a sixth World Cup, he may have to accept another star as talisman.



Vickery believes this will be Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez, hailing his all-round game essential to the national team's success.

Reflecting on the Mauritania win, he told talkSPORT's Trans Europe Express: “With the Argentine national team, my thoughts watching it were, Julian Alvarez played the first half, and he went off at the interval, and Messi came on.



“The conclusion I came away with is, we are now in a situation where Julian Alvarez is much more important to Argentina than Messi is, which seems very strange.

5 Messi finally got his hands on the World Cup at the fifth attempt in 2022 Credit: Getty

5 Julian Alvarez has been tipped to spearhead Argentina's title defence this summer Credit: Getty

“But Messi, the whole thing overshadowed it a little bit. We still don't know if Messi is going to play in the World Cup - this is still an open question.

“The coach, Scaloni, is saying it's up to Messi - it's up to him to decide. He has that right, and he hasn't decided yet.



“So the stadium all want him to do it. It's a kind of love-in.”

Alvarez has established himself as a key player for Argentina in recent years, and scored four goals in their run to World Cup glory in 2022.

He formed a deadly partnership with Messi in Qatar, with the pair combining for all three goals in a 3-0 semi-final win over Croatia.

And Vickery has insisted Alvarez's quality on and off the ball will once again be key to getting the best out of Messi in the summer, should he decide to join Argentina's world title defence.

5 Messi and Alvarez scored a combined 11 goals in Argentina's 2022 World Cup win Credit: Getty

He continued: “Argentina ruined their second half, really, just trying to tee him up for goals, when they should have been playing normally.



“But I think Messi now makes sense alongside Julian Alvarez.

“You take Julian Alvarez away, and just his all-round talent, and the running that he gets through, I think that's now essential to open up space and get Messi firing as well.

“So woe betide anything that happens to Julian Alvarez between now and the World Cup.”

Alvarez registered four goals and three assists in Argentina's World Cup qualifying campaign, while he has 17 goals in all competitions for Atletico Madrid this term, including eight Champions League strikes.

Messi at the 2026 World Cup: What has been said?

Lionel Scaloni revealed in a recent press conference that Messi's participation in the World Cup remains unconfirmed.

Asked if Messi will feature in the summer, the Argentina boss replied: “That’s a question more for him.



5 Lionel Scaloni is gearing up for his second World Cup as Argentina manager, but does not know if he'll be joined by national hero Messi Credit: Getty

“As far as I’m concerned, you already know where I stand. I’ll do everything I can to make sure he’s there. I believe that, for the sake of football, he has to be there.

“It’s not me who decides. It’s up to him, his state of mind, his physical condition.

“It’s difficult because it is not just the Argentinians who want to see him, everyone wants to see him.

“I want him to be there. It’s up to him to decide. He’s earned the right to make that decision with peace of mind. We’re in no rush about it.



“We know whatever he decides will be best for the team and for him. We hope he will be there.”

Football.title: England vs Japan LIVE commentary: Kick-off time and team news as Three Lions continue World Cup prep
Football.content:
England vs Japan LIVE commentary: Kick-off time and team news as Three Lions continue World Cup prep

England welcome Japan to Wembley on Tuesday night as Thomas Tuchel continues his preparations for the World Cup.

The Three Lions were held to a 1-1 draw with Uruguay in London on Friday.

4 White made his first England appearance in more than three years in the draw with Uruguay Credit: Getty

The returning Ben White fired England in front late on, but the spoils were shared after Federico Valverde duly dispatched of a second half injury time penalty.



And England will hope to ramp up their 2026 World Cup prep by returning to winning ways when they face the Samurai Blue.

Japan make the trip south of the border having beaten Scotland 1-0 over the weekend.

Genk forward Junya Ito scored the decisive goal late on as the Far East nation came away from Hampden with a narrow victory.

Tuesday's clash will mark the first time England have faced Japan since claiming a 2-1 win in May 2010.



England vs Japan: Date and how to follow

This international friendly will take place at Wembley on Tuesday, March 31.

The match will kick off at 7:45pm.

talkSPORT will have live commentary of the friendly clash.

4 Junya Ito came off the bench to score Japan's winning goal against Scotland on Saturday Credit: Getty



Adrian Durham presents coverage of at the clash at Wembley, which starts at 7pm on the Kick Off.

Commentary will be provided by Jim Proudfoot and former England captain Stuart Pearce.



Tune in to talkSPORT through the website via the live stream or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

Visit talkSPORT BET for all the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event.

Subscribe to our talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

4 Palmer is hoping to prove his form to earn a spot in England's World Cup squad Credit: Getty



England vs Japan: Team news

The England squad has been hit with further withdrawals following Friday's 1-1 draw with Uruguay.

Noni Madueke was forced off in the first half of the stalemate and has returned to Arsenal.

Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka have also dropped out of the squad and linked back up with the Gunners for 'medical assessments'.

Manchester City pair Phil Foden and John Stones also miss Tuesday's game due to injury, while Adam Wharton, Aaron Ramsdale, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Fikayo Tomori have returned to their respective club sides.

Tuchel has been left with a 27-man squad for Tuesday's game as a result of the high number of withdrawals.



Jude Bellingham will not feature for England.

For Japan, former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu was forced to depart the squad, but is the sole notable exclusion.

Japan came through their 1-0 win over Scotland relatively unscathed, and means manager Hajime Moriyasu has plenty of options for the clash at Wembley.

4 Phil Foden will miss the game against Japan after being forced off due to injury against Uruguay Credit: Getty

England vs Japan: What's been said?

England boss Tuchel insists that the Uruguay experiment went well despite conceding a late equaliser.

"I was looking forward to that match, I tell you. I was looking forward to it because we had some good training sessions and the group was a lively group," Tuchel said.



"I liked the group a lot. I was excited to coach them. I was very happy when I did it. It seemed like we got a win for it. But it was good. It was nice.

"It was nice to see everyone back and we need to make sure that they are ready now against Japan."

Football.title: Tottenham told to re-hire Thomas Frank in shock U-turn
Football.content:
They couldn't, could they?

Arsenal hero Martin Keown has sensationally tipped Tottenham to consider re-hiring Thomas Frank in a last-ditch effort to save their season.

3 The Dane won just 13 of his 38 matches in charge of Tottenham Credit: Getty

Should such a scenario unfold, it would mark Frank's second stint in charge of the north London outfit this term.

The Dane was appointed on a three-year deal last June as Ange Postecoglou's successor despite the Australian ending the club's 17-year major trophy drought.

However, Frank's tenure was cut short after just eight months, with a 2-1 loss to Newcastle proving to be the final straw.

But Tottenham are once again searching for a new manager after Igor Tudor, Frank's replacement, was axed just 43 days into his interim tenure.

Tudor's forgettable reign spanned just seven fixtures, five of which were defeats.

It's left Tottenham, who are 17th and one point clear of the relegation zone in the Premier League, back at square one for the second time in a matter of months.

Given Tudor didn't take long to alienate several Tottenham players, Keown believes whoever replaces the Croatian needs to take a gentler approach towards the squad.

To be Frank

It's why he feels Tottenham could do worse than return to a familiar face, even if Frank was a key reason behind the club being embroiled in the mess it is in now.

"I'm not sure they enjoyed it when the last manager came in, he was quite scathing of the group," Keown said on talkSPORT's White and Jordan.

"Maybe it's an arm around the shoulder a little bit here? It certainly didn't work last time.

3 If Keown had his way, Frank wouldn't be out of work for much longer Credit: Getty

"Look... I know people say you should never go back, but Thomas Frank might be allowed back in the building to actually say, 'Okay, let's try and pick up where we left off'.

"I know that they lost a few games, but it was certainly a lot better than we saw from recent games."

Given Keown's historic affiliation with Tottenham's arch rivals, perhaps his claim needs to be taken with a pinch of salt.

However, given Tottenham are due back in action on April 12 and Frank is available, perhaps there may be method, even if only a slither, to Keown's madness.

De Zerb-ing of a chance?

Despite the idea of a sensational Frank U-turn, talkSPORT understands former Brighton boss Roberto De Zerbi is the main man under consideration from Tottenham to replace Tudor.

De Zerbi is closing in on the job, despite having been initially reluctant to take over before the summer.

3 De Zerbi is available having left Marseille in February Credit: Getty

Key to Tottenham's offer for De Zerbi is the lure of a hefty survival bonus if he preserves the club's Premier League status.

Should De Zerbi be appointed, Tottenham fans will need him to hit the ground running at a quicker pace than he did at Brighton.

The Italian went winless in his first five games in charge of the Seagulls as he oversaw three defeats and two draws.

With just seven league fixtures to go, De Zerbi and Tottenham can ill afford a similar run of results.

News.title: Donald Trump staring down deadly trap to humiliate America into worst nightmare
News.content:
Donald Trump staring down deadly trap to humiliate America into worst nightmare

As US President Donald Trump thrashes out plans for a possible Iran ground invasion experts warns it is a deadly trap set by Tehran to humiliate America and suck it into a guerrilla war

View 6 Images US Marines have been wargaming for a land operation in Diego Garcia (Image: Getty Images)

The US President is about to make the biggest mistake of this war and fall for the deadly trap of ordering thousands of ground troops into Iran.

‌



Almost 20,000 paratroopers and Marines will likely be in place within days for the ‘boots on the ground’ mission aimed at freeing up the Strait of Hormuz and possibly much more.

‌



Several thousand are already in the Gulf, thousands more are on their way and a further deployment of 10,000 is being considered by the Pentagon.

‌



A wave of suicide bombers, missiles, rockets, mines and improvised explosive devices, or roadside bombs awaits an invasion force if it goes ahead.

It may come to a point when all of Trump’s blusters about already having imposed ‘regime change’ and ‘winning the war’ will be pushed aside and he will order his troops to go in.

‌



View 6 Images US President Donald Trump has a huge call to make (Image: Fox News)

And the world’s military experts, commentators and historians are all converging to heed Iranian warnings about setting US forces ‘on fire’ a bold threat but one that should be listened to. This is a trap. A deadly fall-back plan by Iran which always knew it could not take America and Israel on directly.

Instead it has de-centralised its military and prepared for guerrilla warfare, making it impossible to decapitate its potency. And this new regime is more determined, defiant and hard-line than the previous one.

‌



Only this morning a report by former FBI terrorism and Middle East expert Ali Soufan advised that it could lead to ‘fatalities’ and, shudder at the thought, ‘mission creep.’

View 6 Images US air force warplanes have been destroyed by Iran (Image: Twitter/X/sentdefender)

Time and time again politicians have been warned about mission creep, the deadly tendency to pile more troops and resources at a failing conflict that results in inevitable failure.

‌



General Westmoreland headed the US war in Vietnam in the 60’s and famously claimed weekly that the war was being won, whilst demanding ever-more troops.

We know how that ended. The most recent war in Afghanistan was a similar near 20 year conflict, one which embedded the expression ‘mission creep’ in the minds of loved ones of coalition troops sent out there.

We also know how that ended. And yet Trump is sending ever-more ground troops to Iran possibly on a Strait of Hormuz landing mission and perhaps a special forces-led campaign deep inside Iran.

‌



View 6 Images US Marines practise incursion from sea to land (Image: Getty Images)

US President Donald Trump’s latest chaotic declarations about war in Iran pivot from ‘taking Khark Island” to “we’ve had very good negotiations,’ regarding a peace deal.

He has put on hold for the second time his threat of hammering Iran’s infrastructure and energy installations, whilst the Israeli military has pressed on and done just that.

‌



Overnight loud explosions rang throughout Tehran and other major cities and Israel’s military has bragged it is “attacking the infrastructure throughout Tehran.”

The coalition of the US and Israel’s two militaries is diverging by the day as America scrabbles for an off-ramp and Israel seized its moment to inflict as much damage as possible.

View 6 Images In Tehran, vehicles hit by strikes (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The major problem is that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps units and the civilians on the ground too will not distinguish between Israeli and American bombs.

And this means Iran will not trust Trump’s envoys because they have repeatedly held peace talks whilst attacking whilst they were underway.

This operation Epic Fury is a catastrophe running out of control, its purpose and intent lost in the weeks of violence, a situation worsened by Trump’s inability to stop the lying.

Article continues below

Soufan warns in his latest report: ‘Any ground incursion into Iran held territory, even if limited, risks the loss of US personnel to a multiplicity of threats from Iran’s drone and missile arsenal, direct and indirect ground fire, roadside and improvised explosive devices and suicide bombings.

View 6 Images Residents of war-battered Tehran are living among the debris (Image: Getty Images)

“And experts warn that the introduction of ground troops risks ‘mission creep,’ an expansion of the ground operation likely in response to Iran’s reactions to achieve objectives broader than initially envisioned. Some officials worry a small ground offensive has the potential to evolve into a broader operation to capture towns and cities…”

News.title: BREAKING: Thieves steal £9m masterpieces by Renoir, Cézanne and Matisse in 180 seconds
News.content:
A gang of thieves took less than 190 seconds to steal paintings worth an estimated €10m (£8.7m) from a museum in Italy.

That gang made off with the masterpieces by Cézanne, Renoir and Matisse in less than three minutes during the daring raid.

The gang used crowbars to prise open metal bars and gain access to a back entrance of the gallery which housed the Magnani-Rocca Foundation private collection.

The thieves were in the building for less than three minutes before they made their escape across the gardens of the the gallery, which is housed in an elegant palazzo near Parma in the north of Italy.

News.title: Majority of Gen Z ditch nights out for staying in as OAPS 'outpartying them'
News.content:
Majority of Gen Z ditch nights out for staying in as OAPS 'outpartying them'

A survey of 2,000 UK adults by Lamb Weston found millions are swapping busy social calendars for comfort, convenience and quiet nights in at home – especially the younger generation

View Image Over-65s are 'outpartying' Gen Z, according to new research (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

Britain is becoming a nation of stay-at-home enthusiasts as more than six in ten Brits (62%) now prefer a night on the sofa over heading out on the town, new research reveals. The survey of 2,000 UK adults by Lamb Weston found millions are increasingly swapping busy social calendars for comfort, convenience and a quiet evening indoors.

‌



Surprisingly, it's older Brits bucking the trend. Over-65s are now the age group most likely to go out with just 57% saying they prefer staying indoors, compared with more than 60% across every other age bracket. At the other end of the spectrum are young adults who exceed the national average, with 64% of 18-24s expressing a preference for staying at home.

‌



Women (64%) are more likely than men (59%) to opt for a night indoors, the figures show, while people in Cardiff (74%) are the biggest homebodies and those in Birmingham (53%) the most likely to enjoy a night out.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

For many, these quieter evenings are defined by what people describe as "small wins", simple moments that make everyday life feel more manageable.

For example, more than a third of adults (35%) say eating an easy meal at home is one of life's little victories, while going to bed early and finishing work and switching off early (31%) also rank among Britain's top everyday triumphs. The research also reveals that evenings are increasingly about relieving pressure rather than piling on more arrangements. Three in ten (30%) say simply surviving the day with no additional commitments feels like a triumph, while just over a quarter (28%) say remaining in for the evening or enjoying a tranquil night without messages or calls helps them unwind. .

‌



Cancelled plans are also welcomed, with one in five Brits (21%) admitting they feel relieved when social arrangements fall through.

The trend has been dominating TikTok for the past few years, with influencer 'Reece The Realist' posting a video to his 11,500 followers about how the 'new going out is staying in'.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



He was heard saying in the video: "Am I the only one who just can't be bothered to step out anywhere? Even when people shout me, I'll be like, 'Yeah I'm rolling still', however when the day comes, I'm like, 'Nah, I'm not going anywhere.'"

One person replied: "Im the same. I only open the door for deliveries."

While another added: "Bank holiday doing nothing am lying in bed, I can't be bothered."

‌



A third chimed in: "I love being in my house to be fair."

Another video which accumulated hundreds of likes saw TikToker @bridgehouseuk share a video of their home with overlay text reading: 'Do you want to go out tonight?'. As further snaps showed a bubble bath, candles, a record player, roaring fire and their bed, more text read, 'Absolutely not, thank you.'""

One person replied: "It's a no every time." While another chimed in: "Totally agree here!"

Article continues below

As evenings become increasingly home-focused, food habits are evolving as well. Over half of adults (52%) state they regularly choose simpler, quicker meals during the week, while nearly a third (32%) say they actively prioritise meals that are fast and easy to prepare.

Alecia Brown, Marketing Manager at Lamb Weston, commented: "Evenings look different for many people today, with hectic schedules meaning individuals increasingly value time to unwind and savour simple moments at home.

"Our research indicates that small things like an easy dinner or a peaceful evening can feel like real victories after a busy day."

News.title: Man warned pals 'it will go with a bang' before fatal house explosion after rent increase
News.content:
Man warned pals 'it will go with a bang' before fatal house explosion after rent increase

David Howard had lived on John Street, Worksop, for 11 years when the massive explosion reduced the property to rubble on April 12, 2025, killing him and his dog

View 5 Images the explosion in John Street in Worksop demolished the house (Image: PA)

A man's home blew up after he told his friend he'd "pulled off the gas pipes" when his landlord put up the rent by £80.

‌



David Howard had lived at the Nottinghamshire property for 11 years before a massive gas explosion destroyed the house and killed him and his dog.

‌



On April 12, 2025 he received a letter from his landlord saying she was putting up his rent, which was mostly paid by the local council, by £80 to £540.

‌



Friends told how at around 3pm that afternoon Mr Howard started telling several people he was going to "blow the house up", saying "you wait until the end of the day", an inquest into Mr Howard's death was told today.

DC Daniel Akehurst read to the court from an account by one of Mr Howard’s friends, she had told cops that on the day Mr Howard was "p****d off and could not cope anymore" due to his rent going up.

View 5 Images The scene of the explosion on March 27, 2026, almost a year on (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Reach PLC)

‌



Shanelle Williams described how Mr Howard was "in a mood and depressed". The woman was then called by Mr Howard at around 3pm, when he told her "he had pulled the pipes" and made comments about "blowing up the house".

In another call at 3.29pm, Mr Howard told Ms Williams "I’ve done it, I’ve pulled the pipes off the gas. It’s going to go with a bang."

The latter call lasted 42 seconds and was ended by Mr Howard before Ms Williams could say anything. Before this, Mr Howard had told friends he had been up for three days with no sleep and was "very upset" about the rent increase".

‌



A friend tried to give him advice but he wasn’t listening, with Mr Howard saying, "You watch", "You wait until the end of the day" and "You wait to see what happens".

The inquest was told Mr Howard had made similar comments before April 12.

View 5 Images The blast levelled the property (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Reach PLC)

‌



Around 3pm, Mr Howard locked the doors to the property he was renting after two of his friends left to go to a shop, which was described as "strange".

Upon returning, the two friends were told by Mr Howard to "go, I don’t want anyone else to get hurt. Please just go".

Asked by his friends if they could at least take his dog, Roxy, Mr Howard said: "Roxy is staying with me."

‌



Another friend then went to the property and tried speaking to him but was told to “f*** off”. The same person said she could smell gas.

Another then told Mr Howard through the locked door: "You are being stupid, there are kids next door. You are a f****** idiot."

The hearing wasn't told any of the friends made any attempts to notify emergency services of the events.

‌



A call was then received by the police at 7.39pm to say an explosion had occurred at 26 John Street.

View 5 Images David Howard and his dog were killed in the blast (Image: Nottingham post)

DC Akehurst described how the house had "fully collapsed" by the time emergency services arrived to the "chaotic" scene and a major incident was declared.

‌



The hearing was told up to 200 people were "milling around" the street, with these residents then evacuated.

DC Akehurst said the explosion was "large and powerful" and its force had also damaged the adjacent properties, as well as some opposite.

A statement from a first responder read out in the hearing said Mr Howard was still conscious when emergency services arrived and reported having significant difficulty breathing and "was slowly being crushed" as he was "trapped under a significant amount of rubble".

‌



Crew couldn't get to him, however, due to the difficulty of the scene and he was pronounced dead at 9.58pm.

Christopher Trendowicz, fire investigator at Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service, told the hearing that the explosion happened on the ground floor of the property, with its upper floor collapsing on top.

The Health and Safety Executive (HSE) instructed gas company Cadent to investigate any possible leaks from outside the property but this was not the case.

‌



View 5 Images the explosion in John Street in Worksop demolished the house (Image: PA)

The gas meter, boiler and piping were also tested and found to be safe.

The only abnormality found was damage to the cooker, owned by Mr Howard, which had its flexible gas pipe "stretched to capacity".

‌



Mr Trendowicz said this was the likely cause of the gas leak, with the likely cause for the ignition being the capacitator of the fridge/freezer in the property being "ripped out".

The fridge/freezer was found away from where it would be ordinarily, the hearing was told.

Coroner Nathanael Hartley concluded Mr Howard's cause of death as 1a asphyxia whilst entrapped beneath collapsed building debris and 2 heroin and cocaine use.

‌



Mr Howard had low levels of the two drugs and alcohol in his blood at the time of his death, which could have led to "mild cognitive impairment".

He had a history of mental health issues, having been diagnosed with PTSD and moderate depression in 2021, as well as a substance abuse misuse history, which he first reported in 2012.

Mr Howard's two daughters, Keely and Lauren Howard, both attended the hearing but refused to comment on their father's mental health or to describe him as a person when asked by coroner Hartley.

Article continues below

No notes were recovered from the property during the investigation, coroner Hartley said.

The coroner said: "Having heard the evidence from the fire service about the damaged gas pipe cooker and the evidence that David had informed his friend that he had 'pulled the pipes, was going to blow the house up and it was going to go with a bang', I find that David caused the damage to the gas cooker intentionally.

"It's possible that David did not appreciate the dangerousness of the situation. With that in mind, I do not find that David intended to end his life when he did. I find that David's intentions cannot be established."

News.title: Meghan and Harry's 'crossroads' - Netflix row, dimming spark and UK gamble
News.content:
Meghan and Harry's 'crossroads' - Netflix row, dimming spark and UK gamble

As Prince Harry apparently eyes up an unexpected 'family time' trip to the UK, an expert warns that he and wife Meghan Markle are currently navigating a tricky "crossroads" in life

View 6 Images Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are said to be navigating a 'crossroads' (Image: Amy Katz/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Nearly eight years after their fairytale wedding, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have reportedly reached a crossroads, and an unexpected summer plan could change everything.

‌



On May 19, 2018, crowds gathered in Windsor to celebrate the wedding of Harry and Meghan, with guests gathering in the historic St George's Chapel to watch the happy couple say, 'I do'. It was a glamorous affair, combining the newlyweds' respective worlds of royalty and Hollywood. The likes of George and Amal Clooney lined the pews, while King Charles III, then still Prince of Wales, proudly walked his new daughter-in-law down the aisle, in place of her now estranged father, Thomas Markle.

‌



A glittering and joyous occasion, set against bright blue May skies, nobody could have guessed what would come to pass less than two years later. On January 8, 2020, the UK woke up to the news that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex would be stepping back from their roles as senior members of the Royal Family, and would be carving out financially independent lives for themselves beyond the palace walls.

‌



A new life in Montecito, California, beckoned, and with it, Netflix deals, podcasts and bombshell interviews, their most notable being a sit-down chat with Oprah Winfrey. Here, the couple spoke openly about the tensions that had erupted within the seemingly united House of Windsor behind closed doors, with a particular focus on Harry's strained relationship with father, Charles, and brother Prince William.

The years since have done nothing to thaw the ice across the Atlantic Ocean, with Harry's explosive 2023 bombshell, Spare, viewed as the final nail in the coffin by many Royal watchers. However, there are whispers that all is not lost yet, with Harry reportedly hoping for a UK visit at a pivotal time in his life.

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle scolded in brutal takedown by former prime minister READ MORE :

View 6 Images The Sussexes struck out on their own in January 2020 and have built a new life in America (Image: AP)

‌



As reported by The Sunday Times, despite their widely publicised disagreements, Harry, 41, is keen to visit his beloved father Charles, who is still living with an undisclosed form of cancer, and hopes to receive an invitation to Sandringham this summer. The Duke of Sussex is reportedly keen for some "family time", and longs to bring Meghan, 44, and their two children, Prince Archie, six, and Princess Lilibet, four.

It will have been four long years since the little prince and princess, who are being raised over in America, saw their paternal grandfather. Meanwhile, mum-of-two Meghan hasn't visited the UK since the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II in September 2022. It's clear that such a reunion would mark a huge step forward for the divided family, but it's not quite as simple as booking plane tickets.

Harry is understood to be waiting for a decision regarding his security in the UK, with the Sussexes having been stripped of their right to armed police protection following the so-called "Megxit". The Duke has repeatedly asserted that, until this royal protection is reinstated, he does not feel safe bringing his young family across the pond.

‌



However, it's thought that an invitation to Norfolk from Charles, 77, could enable Harry to bring Meghan, Archie and Lili along on the trip. A pal of Harry’s told the publication: “If he was invited by the King, he would get a package of security that automatically kicks in. He’d like an invite to Sandringham. Would he go? It would depend who was there. If the King was to say, ‘Come up and spend some time with the family’, he’d love that.”

View 6 Images Meghan hasn't been back to the UK since Queen Elizabeth's funeral in Septmeber 2022 (Image: Netflix)

‌



Harry and Charles last saw each other on September 10, at Clarence House, for a 50-minute tea, marking their first meeting in 19 months. It's understood they've spoken several times since, but haven't seen each other face to face, a prospect that Harry would "love" to come to pass. However, such an event will, of course, all depend on security.

The source continued: “There is not a world in which he brings the kids back unless there is an enhanced security package around them. If the King wants to see the kids, all he needs to do is invite them over and it can happen. It is up to the King, unless Ravec do the right thing independently of the King and decide he requires an enhanced package of security, so he can stay as long as he wants whenever he wants, and see his father with the children. There are lots of scenarios to make it work, but it’s all out of Harry’s hands. No father would want to put their kids at any risk.”

While Charles spends his summers at Balmoral, he often spends time at Sandringham in July first, and so it can be assumed that this is the month such a long- awaited visit would take place. These reports come at a supposed "crossroads" for Harry and Meghan, who are allegedly seeing some cracks in their glossy American dream.

‌

We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Royal newsletter here to get all the biggest royal news and exclusive pictures, straight to your inbox.

View 6 Images Harry longs to see his father, but only if he can ensure his young family's safety

It's believed by some that the shine could be coming off the once sought-after Sussex brand, with British population polls showing a steady decline . In the latest YouGov.com polls, just 19 per cent of people had a positive view of Meghan - her lowest ranking yet - while Harry came in at 31 per cent, significantly lower than brother Prince William's 77 per cent.

‌



While Meghan's Netflix series, With Love, Meghan, and As Ever range of wines and jams have brought in the cash, with an astonishing value of $250m (£185m), popularity will be needed in the long term to keep her brands coveted. Now, PR guru Mayah Riaz believes the couple has reached a crucial turning point on the road, and a "clear lane" ahead will be needed to keep the ship steady.

Ms Riaz previously told the Mirror: "Harry and Meghan no longer have the institutional weight of the monarchy behind them. Without that framework, they are competing in a very crowded celebrity marketplace. In today's world, star power alone is not enough. You need a clear lane and a compelling reason for people to keep watching.

"They are still globally recognised, and that is a powerful asset. But relevance today is not about titles. It is about consistency, credibility and connection. In terms of the Andrew scandal creating space for them, I think that was always a risky assumption. Controversy within the royal family does not automatically translate into opportunity for those outside it. If anything, what we see is that the public often rallies around stability in turbulent moments."

‌



View 6 Images Netflix has now parted ways with Meghan's lifestyle brand, As Ever. (Image: Netflix)

When the Sussexes' five-year Netflix deal came to an end last summer, it was announced that their contract was being downgraded to a less lucrative "first look deal", giving the streaming giant first refusal on any new projects. Then, earlier this month, it was announced that Netflix would be parting ways with Meghan's lifestyle brand As Ever. Now, scathing reports in Variety suggest the relationship between the Sussexes and Netflix is "done". As per the showbiz bible, certain decisions from the couple - including their Oprah interview - "blindsided" bosses. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have strongly denied the claims.

Stock was reportedly a concern for Netflix, with the publication claiming that last August, Netflix was "sitting on a surplus of As Ever products, including tea and baking mixes, totalling more than $10 million in value". The magazine also alleged that the company began "giving inventory to employees for free, putting the goods on card tables in various office buildings". In response, an Archewell spokesperson stated that giveaways from sample closets are regarded as standard practice at studios.

‌



Meanwhile, there have also been questions regarding the supposedly mixed messages the Sussexes are sending out. While they've long called for privacy for themselves and their children, Meghan surprised many by increasingly featuring blurred images of Archie and Lilibet in photos for brand promotions. In one snap, half of Lilibet's face was visible, in a move some believe wouldn't sit well with protective dad Harry at all.

View 6 Images Archie and Lilibet regularly feature in mum Meghan's Instagram promotions

On this note, royal expert and author Ingrid Seward told the Mirror : "They have completely ignored the fact that they said they were leaving the royal family because they wanted a more private life, and they have created anything but that for themselves. It appears they left the family because they wanted a public life and to earn money."

‌



Having built an empire off their royal lineage, the Sussexes are now in an in-between state, straddling the philanthropic pursuits Harry honed during his time in the palace, and Meghan's more recent endeavours as a lifestyle guru and entrepreneur. Ms Riaz told us: "Ultimately, they are at a crossroads. They can either lean fully into being global philanthropists with measurable impact, or fully embrace lifestyle entrepreneurship and own it unapologetically. Sitting between the two is what I think creates the confusion. And in the current media climate, confusion is the quickest route to indifference."

Now independent from Netflix, there are hints as to where Meghan will be taking her As Ever brand next, with some speculating she could have her eye on Australia. A source recently told the Telegraph: "We are thinking about the next step in global expansion and Australia has been teed up as the first test market outside the US. It's the first place we are looking at and having conversations. They have to earn a living. They are private citizens and have to pay the bills like anyone else."

In response, a Sussex spokesperson said: "This is speculation. No decisions have been made about when or where international expansion might take place. Entering new markets is a considered process, but it's something the brand is excited to explore as it continues to grow in this next phase. Watch this space."

Article continues below

Eagle-eyed royal watchers have noted that Harry and Meghan will be heading to Oz just next month to partake in "private, business and philanthropic engagements". This marks their first trip to Oz since October 2018. During this trip, Meghan will appear at a £1,400 per person 'girls' weekend' in Sydney, led by Her Best Life podcast founder Gemma O'Neill. Running from April 17 to April 19, the event, which centres around "powerful conversations, relaxation, laughter, and unforgettable experiences", will see Meghan and Gemma discuss "life, parenting, relationships, building a global business and navigating a public persona".

News.title: Airline bans influencer and plans to launch legal claim over what he did on plane
News.content:
Airline bans influencer and plans to launch legal claim over what he did on plane

Yeferson Cossio, who boasts more than 12m Instagram followers, could face legal action after making excessive flatulence sounds on an international flight

View 3 Images Cossio has millions of followers (Image: JamPress)

An influencer could face legal action over what he is said to have done on an international flight.

‌



Yeferson Cossio, who boasts 12.5m Instagram followers, was allegedly filming the prank for social media content but is yet to post the video after airline Avianca banned him from the return flight.

‌



The prank took place on a flight from Bogotá in Colombia to Madrid, Spain, earlier this month where the Colombian influencer allegedly used a machine that produced realistic flatulent sounds and an unpleasant odour.

‌



According to reports, one female traveller was deeply offended by the stunt. And now the airline plans to take action against the influencer, it said a statement released yesterday.

View 3 Images Cossio was banned from the airline (Image: JamPress)

UK weather maps turn bright yellow for 20C scorcher after Easter bank holiday READ MORE :

They referenced section 8.6 of their terms and conditions related to “conduct that affects safety, comfort, order and discipline on the aircraft”. They said the prank was carried out while the aircraft was flying over the Atlantic Ocean, on March 11, during a part of the journey where an emergency landing was not possible to due to the distance to the nearest airport.

‌



The company stressed that in a closed environment, with a pressurised air recirculation system, this type of act poses a direct risk to other passengers. They also said that the influencer was seen activating the machine with the intention of eliciting reactions from other travellers in the cabin.

View 3 Images Cossio has not issued a statement (Image: JamPress)

They added: “Avianca categorically rejects any behaviour that jeopardises the safety of its operations and compromises the onboard experience for customers and service personnel.” As of today, Cossio has not issued a statement regarding the legal action announced by the airline.

‌



He hit the headlines in 2023 when he underwent an “excruciating” leg-lengthening operation to be several inches taller. The influencer, who used to be 5’8” (1.77m) tall, is now officially 6’07” (1.85m), as reported by Creatorzine.com.

At the time, he told his followers: “I underwent the most painful surgery in the entire world. Just as it’s the most painful operation, it is also one of the most expensive.”

Cossio had to rely on the aid of crutches and a wheelchair to move around for over a year. However, the tattooed influencer, who boasts a luxury lifestyle and fleet of high-end cars, said he is now back to normal.

Article continues below

Cossio, who comes from Antioquia, Colombia, said he wanted to undergo the operation because he broke both his legs in an accident many years ago and has never been right since.

News.title: Top 10 lucky charms Brits swear by for good fortune - and colour matters
News.content:
Top 10 lucky charms Brits swear by for good fortune - and colour matters

Brits have revealed the top 10 items they rely on for good fortune when they need a little bit of extra luck

View 2 Images Brits admit they rely on certain items to help bring them good luck (Image: Getty Images)

Socks, sentimental jewellery and a specific pair of shoes are among the lucky charms Brits swear by when they want fortune on their side. A poll of 2,000 adults found 54% believe what they wear can directly influence their luck whether in job interviews (41%) or exams and tests (26%).

‌



The research found 10% rely on a trusty pair of pants while 11% will go with anything, if it’s proven lucky in the past. More than one in five (22%) have even changed an outfit at the last minute because what they were already wearing felt ‘unlucky’.

‌



It turns out one in 10 (11%) associate the colour green with winning and good fortune, with black and brown most associated as unlucky clothing colours.

‌



View 2 Images Brits associate the colour green with good luck (Image: Getty Images)

The research was commissioned by The Birthday Draw, where entrants can choose a colour, date and an initial to create their entry and could win a £1 million jackpot.

More than half (55%) of those polled believe a lucky outfit makes them feel more in control, according to the OnePoll.com data. Around one in four (27%) have attributed a success or win directly to what they were wearing at the time.

‌



With 47%, at one point or another, having won a competition or prize purely based on luck, and not skill, as 31% consider themselves lucky in general.

The study found that of those with a lucky item of clothing, 30% have avoided washing it in case they ‘washed the luck away’. As many as one in 10 of these have stretched this process out and have avoided putting their lucky charm in the wash for longer than two weeks.

The research discovered three quarters claim that what they wear can directly impact their confidence. With the same percentage (76%) saying feeling confident improves their chances of success overall.

Article continues below

Nikki Cooper, spokesperson for The Birthday Draw, added: “It’s no surprise that many believe their outfit choices can influence their luck, be it wearing a certain colour or personalised jewellery.

“These small rituals provide a huge boost in confidence and a sense of control that make us feel extra lucky.”

News.title: Race Across The World star opens up about 'emotional' health battle after infertility struggle
News.content:
Race Across The World star opens up about 'emotional' health battle after infertility struggle

Betty Mukherjee has opened up about a condition she discovered when she was a teenager, leaving her spending thousands on complex procedures in the hopes of becoming a mother

View 3 Images Betty Mukherjee has opened up on her health diagnosis (Image: Studio Lambert)

A rising BBC star has revealed her secret health battle that left her worried she would never be a mother. Betty Mukherjee, who found fame on Race Across the World alongside her brother James, has shared how being born without a womb has impacted everything from her confidence to her relationships.

‌



The 28-year-old lives with MRKH syndrome - a rare condition that affects the reproductive system - and was diagnosed as a teenager after realising something wasn't right. While her friends began getting their periods, hers never came. A visit to her GP at just 16 led to a life-changing diagnosis that would alter how she viewed her future.

‌



"My first reaction was shock more than anything," she said. "I don’t think I fully processed it in that moment." But as she grew older, the full weight of what it meant began to sink in.

‌



Doctor shares five simple steps to 'heal' your body READ MORE :

Don't ignore small symbol on sunscreen bottles this spring READ MORE :

View 3 Images Betty Mukherjee appeared on Race Across The World with her brother (Image: Studio Lambert)

MRKH syndrome, also known as Rokitansky syndrome, means Betty was born without a fully developed uterus. She also has only one kidney. While the condition is invisible to others, she has described the emotional burden it carries as anything but.

Growing up, she was forced to confront complex conversations about fertility, relationships and identity far earlier than most of her peers. And with women already facing the pressure of an internal "body clock", this only added to her anxiety.

‌



She has spoken about the "quiet insecurity" she carried for years, particularly when it came to dating and opening up about her condition. Sharing such personal information early in relationships brought fear and uncertainty, but she has since found a more confident and open approach.

Now in a long-term relationship with partner Dan, Betty says she has found unwavering support as she navigates her fertility journey. The couple have begun IVF treatment in the hope of creating embryos that could one day allow them to start a family through surrogacy or a potential womb transplant.

Their first round of treatment, completed in October 2025, resulted in two healthy embryos. A second round has recently been completed, with the couple hoping to reach the number required to be considered for a transplant programme.

‌



View 3 Images Betty Mukherjee lives with a rare condition (Image: Studio Lambert)

The process, however, has come at a significant financial cost. Their first cycle was privately funded and totalled just under £13,000 once medication, egg collection and embryo creation were included. While they have since secured NHS support for further treatment, additional testing still comes at a price.

Fertility treatment is rarely straightforward, and Betty has been open about the emotional highs and lows that come with it. "IVF and fertility treatment can bring a lot of uncertainty, and hope can sometimes feel fragile," she told The Sun.

‌



She described moments where the experience feels overwhelming, balanced by a deep sense of gratitude that medical advances have created options that simply didn't exist before.

Despite the challenges, she remains determined to become a mother - even if the path looks different from what she once imagined. For Betty, coming to terms with not being able to carry her own child has been a gradual process.

Being told as a teenager that pregnancy was not an option left her feeling isolated at times, but she has since found comfort in the idea that there are many ways to build a family.

‌



"Motherhood has always been something I’ve imagined in my future," she said. Rather than focusing on traditional expectations, she now sees it as something defined by care, love and stability.

By speaking openly, Betty has also become a source of support for others living with the same condition. She has revealed she regularly receives messages from women and girls who had previously felt alone, many saying they had never heard MRKH discussed so openly before.

The response has reinforced her belief in the importance of talking about women’s health - particularly conditions that are often misunderstood or rarely spoken about.

Article continues below

She hopes that by sharing her story, others will feel less isolated and more empowered to understand their own bodies. While her time on television saw her travel across continents, Betty says her most important journey is only just beginning.

The road to motherhood may be uncertain, expensive and emotionally demanding, but it is one she is determined to continue.
